extracted.intended_audience: respondents and practitioners involved in USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) disciplinary proceedings; patent practitioners facing OED complaints
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural standards governing default judgment in USPTO OED disciplinary proceedings when a respondent fails to file a timely answer, including service, deadlines, notice, and the regulatory basis for entry of default and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file timely answer equals admission and may lead to default judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: "USPTO regulations state that a failure to file a timely answer constitutes an admission of all allegations and 'may result in entry of default judgment.' 37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent does not file a timely answer to the Complaint, the allegations may be treated as admitted and the OED may move for entry of default judgment; where no response is filed, the Default Motion will be granted (as in this matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority for the proceeding and decision
rubrics_metrics.description: "This Court is authorized to hear this proceeding and to issue this Initial Decision pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§11.19 and 11.39."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Law Judges (here, HUD ALJs under an interagency agreement) have statutory/regulatory authority to adjudicate OED matters and issue initial decisions pursuant to cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Complaint and notice of answer deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint was mailed via U.S. certified mail and e-mailed to respondent; the mailed Complaint was signed for. The Complaint notified respondent that he had 30 days to file a response and that a decision by default may be entered if a written answer is not timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of mailing/receipt (e.g., signed certified mail) and e-mailing constitute service for purposes of triggering the 30-day answer deadline; the due date is computed from date of service (in this case answer due no later than November 7, 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up notice and opportunity to avoid default
rubrics_metrics.description: On November 13, 2013, the OED Director sent Respondent a letter informing Respondent that no answer had been received, and that the OED Director would seek a default judgment unless Respondent responded by November 22, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED may send additional notice warning of an impending default and provide a short cure period; failure to respond to such follow-up notices supports entry of default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion practice and consequence — default motion leads to disciplinary sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government filed a Motion for Entry of Default Judgment and Imposition of Disciplinary Sanction on December 5, 2013; because Respondent did not file any response, the Default Motion will be GRANTED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where motion for default is filed after unresponded-to Complaint and follow-up notices, the tribunal may grant the motion and proceed to impose disciplinary sanctions consistent with the regulations and the admitted allegations.
